broca.summary: French surgeon who, through the case of the patient known as "Tan," linked speech production to the left frontal lobe

wernicke.summary: German neuropsychiatrist who described temporal lobe damage affecting speech comprehension

geschwind.summary: American neurologist who revived and systematized behavioral neurology and disconnection syndromes

penfield.summary: Canadian neurosurgeon who used electrical stimulation to map functional areas of the human cortex

cajal.summary: Spanish histologist who used silver staining to show that neurons are independent cells

waldeyer.summary: German anatomist who formally introduced the term "neuron" in 1891

lorenz.summary: Austrian ethologist who shared the Nobel Prize with Tinbergen and others for his work on imprinting

tinbergen.summary: Dutch ethologist who proposed four questions for the study of behavior

selye.summary: Canadian endocrinologist who brought the word "stress" into medicine and everyday language

cannon.summary: American physiologist who proposed the "fight or flight" response and the concept of homeostasis

mcewen.summary: American neuroendocrinologist who proposed the concept of allostatic load

shelley-taylor.summary: American social psychologist who proposed the "tend and befriend" response to stress, and co-wrote "Social Cognition" with Fiske

hebb.summary: Canadian psychologist who proposed the learning rule that synapses strengthen with repeated co-activation

bliss.summary: British neuroscientist who, with Lomo, discovered long-term potentiation

lomo.summary: Norwegian neurophysiologist who, with Bliss, discovered long-term potentiation

delay.summary: French psychiatrist who, with Deniker, reported the effects of chlorpromazine on psychosis

deniker.summary: French psychiatrist who, with Delay, helped found psychopharmacology

carlsson.summary: Swedish pharmacologist who showed that dopamine is a neurotransmitter and proposed the dopamine hypothesis of psychosis

schildkraut.summary: American psychiatrist who proposed the catecholamine hypothesis of depression

scoville.summary: American neurosurgeon who removed the medial temporal lobes of patient H.M.

milner.summary: British-born Canadian neuropsychologist who studied patient H.M. in depth and helped establish a multi-system view of memory

squire.summary: American neuroscientist who distinguished declarative from procedural memory

luria.summary: Soviet neuropsychologist who systematized the case study of brain injury and methods of assessment

plomin.summary: British behavioral geneticist who has long studied the genetic basis of intelligence and personality

bouchard.summary: American psychologist who directed the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart

sperry.summary: American neuroscientist who received the 1981 Nobel Prize for his split-brain research

gazzaniga.summary: American neuroscientist who studied split-brain patients and is one of the founders of cognitive neuroscience

bogen.summary: American neurosurgeon who performed early corpus callosotomy operations and worked with Sperry

kandel.summary: American neuroscientist who studied the molecular mechanisms of learning in sea slugs and won the 2000 Nobel Prize

crick.summary: British molecular biologist who in later life turned to studying consciousness through vision

koch.summary: German-American neuroscientist who worked with Crick on the neural correlates of consciousness

charles-darwin.summary: British naturalist who proposed the theory of natural selection and also wrote "The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals"

hamilton.summary: British evolutionary biologist who proposed kin selection theory

trivers.summary: American evolutionary biologist who proposed theories of reciprocal altruism and parental investment

cosmides.summary: American psychologist and one of the main founders of evolutionary psychology

tooby.summary: American anthropologist who co-founded evolutionary psychology with Cosmides

buss.summary: American psychologist who studies mate preferences and sex differences through an evolutionary lens

damasio.summary: Portuguese-born American neurologist who proposed the somatic marker hypothesis

ledoux.summary: American neuroscientist who studies fear and the amygdala circuits that underlie it

panksepp.summary: Estonian-born American neuroscientist who proposed a set of basic emotional systems

ekman.summary: American psychologist who studied facial expressions and the cross-cultural universality of emotion

barrett.summary: American psychologist who proposed the theory of constructed emotion

sapolsky.summary: American neuroendocrinologist who studies the biology of stress and behavior and is known for popular science writing

thorndike.summary: American psychologist who proposed the law of effect based on puzzle-box experiments, and a founder of educational psychology

pavlov.summary: Russian physiologist who won the Nobel Prize for his research on digestion, and is known for his work on conditioned reflexes

watson.summary: American psychologist who proclaimed behaviorism and later moved into the advertising industry

rayner.summary: American psychologist who collaborated with Watson on the "Little Albert" study

rescorla.summary: American psychologist who proposed that conditioning depends on how well a signal predicts the outcome

wagner.summary: American psychologist who worked with Rescorla to develop an associative learning model

garcia.summary: American psychologist who discovered taste aversion learning and the biological preparedness of learning

tolman.summary: American psychologist who proposed cognitive maps and latent learning

hull.summary: American psychologist whose mathematical drive-reduction theory dominated learning research in the 1940s

skinner.summary: American psychologist who founded operant conditioning and radical behaviorism

ferster.summary: American psychologist who co-authored "Schedules of Reinforcement" with Skinner

herrnstein.summary: American psychologist who proposed the matching law and later became known for "The Bell Curve"

wolpe.summary: South African-born American psychiatrist who developed systematic desensitization

bandura.summary: Canadian-born American psychologist who proposed observational learning and self-efficacy, linking behaviorist and cognitive traditions

seligman.summary: American psychologist who moved from research on learned helplessness to positive psychology

baer.summary: American psychologist and one of the founders of applied behavior analysis

wolf.summary: American psychologist and one of the founders of applied behavior analysis, who developed the "Teaching-Family" model

risley.summary: American psychologist who, with Baer and Wolf, defined applied behavior analysis and later studied children's language environments

lovaas.summary: Norwegian-born American psychologist and early advocate of intensive behavioral intervention for autism

fechner.summary: German physicist and philosopher who founded psychophysics

e-h-weber.summary: German physiologist who found that the just noticeable difference in sensation is proportional to stimulus intensity

wundt.summary: German psychologist who founded the first psychology laboratory in Leipzig

titchener.summary: English-born American student of Wundt who advocated structuralism and introspection

donders.summary: Dutch physiologist who devised the subtraction method for analyzing mental processes through reaction times

ebbinghaus.summary: German psychologist who was the first to study memory experimentally

james.summary: American philosopher and psychologist, author of "The Principles of Psychology" and a leading figure of pragmatism

wertheimer.summary: German psychologist and founder of Gestalt psychology

koffka.summary: German psychologist and one of the three founders of Gestalt psychology

kohler.summary: German psychologist known for his experiments on insight in chimpanzees

bartlett.summary: British psychologist who proposed schemas and reconstructive memory

miller.summary: American psychologist, a central figure in the cognitive revolution and author of "The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two"

broadbent.summary: British psychologist who studied attention using the metaphor of an information channel

chomsky.summary: American linguist who used linguistic arguments to refute the behaviorist account of language

neisser.summary: American psychologist, author of "Cognitive Psychology," who later criticized laboratory cognitive research for lacking ecological validity

atkinson.summary: American psychologist and co-proposer of the multi-store model of memory

shiffrin.summary: American psychologist and co-proposer of the multi-store model of memory

baddeley.summary: British psychologist who proposed the model of working memory

kahneman.summary: Israeli-American psychologist who received the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for prospect theory

tversky.summary: Israeli-American psychologist who, with Kahneman, founded the study of judgment and decision-making

gigerenzer.summary: German psychologist who criticized explanations of human irrationality and advocated ecological rationality

loftus.summary: American psychologist who studies eyewitness testimony and false memories

schacter.summary: American psychologist who studies memory errors and implicit memory

rumelhart.summary: American psychologist, a founder of connectionism and a co-developer of the backpropagation algorithm

mcclelland.summary: American psychologist who worked with Rumelhart to develop the parallel distributed processing model

pinker.summary: Canadian-born American cognitive scientist and popular science writer who criticized connectionist models of language

lakoff.summary: American cognitive linguist who proposed the theory of conceptual metaphor

varela.summary: Chilean biologist and neuroscientist, a proponent of embodied mind and enactive cognition

rosch.summary: American cognitive psychologist who proposed prototype theory of categories and contributed to "The Embodied Mind"

gibson.summary: American perceptual psychologist who proposed ecological perception and affordances

friston.summary: British neuroscientist who proposed the free energy principle

dayan.summary: British computational neuroscientist who studies reinforcement learning and computational psychiatry

dolan.summary: British psychiatrist and neuroscientist who studies the brain mechanisms of decision-making and emotion

bransford.summary: American cognitive scientist and a leading advocate of the learning sciences, and co-editor of "How People Learn"

ann-brown.summary: American developmental and educational psychologist who studied metacognition and reciprocal teaching

galton.summary: British polymath and cousin of Darwin who pioneered the study of individual differences and proposed eugenics

pearson.summary: British statistician who gave the mathematical form of the correlation coefficient and was also an advocate of eugenics

spearman.summary: British psychologist who proposed the general intelligence factor g and developed factor analysis

thurstone.summary: American psychologist who developed multiple factor analysis and the concept of "primary mental abilities"

cattell.summary: British-born American psychologist who proposed fluid and crystallized intelligence and the 16 personality factors

carroll.summary: American psychologist who built a three-stratum model of intelligence through a large-scale reanalysis of data

binet.summary: French psychologist who designed the first practical intelligence scale

simon.summary: French physician who collaborated with Binet on the Binet-Simon scale
